<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The three aspects of Yaakov's journey are present in every Jew, as the deeds of the fathers empower the children, especially regarding Yaakov.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the three above-mentioned matters that were in Yaakov –</t>
    <t s="2">(a)</t>
    <t s="3">his departure from Be'er Sheva to Charan,</t>
    <t s="4">(b)</t>
    <t s="5">his service</t>
    <t s="6">(after the departure from Be'er Sheva)</t>
    <t s="7">"And he took from the stones of the place, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="8">(c)</t>
    <t s="9">(that through his prayer)</t>
    <t s="10">this stone</t>
    <t s="11">(which he took from the stones of the place)</t>
    <t s="12">became the house of G-d – exist also in each and every Jew.</t>
    <t s="13">For "the deeds of the fathers are a sign and give power to the children"</t>
    <t s="14">(as above, section 2),</t>
    <t s="15">and especially the matters of Yaakov.</t>
    <t s="16">For since "the beauty of Yaakov is like the beauty of Adam HaRishon,"</t>
    <t s="17">and his soul includes all the souls of Israel</t>
    <t s="18">(like the soul of Adam HaRishon),</t>
    <t s="19">therefore the service of Yaakov</t>
    <t s="20">("And he took from the stones of the place, etc.")</t>
    <t s="21">gives power to the children with greater excellence and greater strength.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The departure of the soul from its lofty source to the body is empowered by an oath to be righteous, enabling its service below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">The explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that "And Yaakov departed from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan" refers</t>
    <t s="2">to the descent of the soul into the body,</t>
    <t s="3">that it descended from a high</t>
    <t s="4">peak</t>
    <t s="5">(Be'er Sheva)</t>
    <t s="6">to a deep pit</t>
    <t s="7">(Charan).</t>
    <t s="8">And just as Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="9">in order to be able to go to Charan, was drawn a more elevated power – the matter of "Command the salvations of Yaakov"</t>
    <t s="10">(as above, section 5),</t>
    <t s="11">so too is it regarding the "and he went to Charan" in each and every Jew,</t>
    <t s="12">that before the descent of the soul below into the deep pit,</t>
    <t s="13">which is the matter of "and he went to Charan,"</t>
    <t s="14">they give it a special power so that it can perform its service of refining the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world.</t>
    <t s="15">And as is known</t>
    <t s="16">regarding the matter of "they adjure him: 'Be righteous and do not be wicked.'"</t>
    <t s="17">And this is the meaning of "And Yaakov departed from Be'er Sheva, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="18">that the explanation of "Be'er Sheva" is</t>
    <t s="19">that which they adjure him: "Be righteous, etc."</t>
    <t s="20">[There are three explanations of this:</t>
    <t s="21">an oath,</t>
    <t s="22">satiety and seven,</t>
    <t s="23">as explained in many places]</t>
    <t s="24">which is a special empowerment for the service of the soul in its descent below.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The soul's service below consists of Torah and mitzvos, which elevate it, and the refinement of the body and animal soul through all one's actions being for G-d's sake.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the service of the soul in its descent below is</t>
    <t s="2">(generally)</t>
    <t s="3">in two matters.</t>
    <t s="4">First,</t>
    <t s="5">the study of Torah and the fulfillment of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="6">for specifically through the study of Torah and fulfillment of the mitzvos below, the soul is elevated higher than it was before its descent.</t>
    <t s="7">And as is known,</t>
    <t s="8">the Torah and mitzvos specifically below become a garment for the soul in the Garden of Eden, through which it apprehends and delights in the Ein Sof.</t>
    <t s="9">And second,</t>
    <t s="10">the refinement of the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world.</t>
    <t s="11">This is accomplished through the fulfillment of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="12">and even more so – through the service of "all your deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven,"</t>
    <t s="13">and especially through "in all your ways know Him,"</t>
    <t s="14">that not only should his permissible actions be for the sake of Heaven,</t>
    <t s="15">but that even in them themselves</t>
    <t s="16">(in all your ways)</t>
    <t s="17">there should be "know Him"</t>
    <t s="18">[knowledge of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="19">for "knowledge" is higher even than wisdom,</t>
    <t s="20">as explained at length in the continuation of the discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek</t>
    <t s="21">and in many places].</t>
    <t s="22">And this is "and He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear, and I will return in peace to my father's house,"</t>
    <t s="23">"bread to eat and a garment to wear" refers to the study of Torah and the fulfillment of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="24">as is known,</t>
    <t s="25">that Torah is bread and food for the soul, and the mitzvos are garments for the soul,</t>
    <t s="26">and "I will return in peace" is the matter of the work of refinement.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
